$notes.deny-vs-guard: The deny list catches the obvious shapes cheaply and applies in every permission mode. The guard hook catches what a glob cannot -- environment-variable prefixes, pipes, encoded payloads, remote connection strings. Both exist because either alone is porous.
$notes.not-a-boundary: None of this is a security boundary. It is a mistake-catcher. The real boundary is that production write credentials do not exist on this machine and the production role has no write grants.
$notes.no-ask-rules: Trellis ships NO ask rules, deliberately. They apply in every permission mode, so a user who has explicitly opted out of prompts still gets them - surprising and paternalistic. And a prompt clicked through twenty times a day teaches people to click through prompts, which costs exactly the attention the load-bearing ones need. The protection here is the deny list and the guard hook, neither of which can be clicked past. Wanting confirmation before commits is a preference, and preferences belong to the person, not the framework - put an ask list in your personal settings.
